title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory study that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator when evaluating LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we executed Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These artifact-grounded outcomes lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We (1) release the preregistered design and run accounting in an archived execution manifest, (2) explain why a near-zero marginal gain was observed in this constrained regime, and (3) identify boundary conditions where guarded emulation remains likely to add operational value.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and NetOps workflows. Safe operational use demands that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow-ordering constraints, and higher-order invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up). A common operational architecture layers generation with automated validation (deterministic validators), optional repair, and—sometimes—sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only violations that static checks miss. Prior surveys and prototype systems recommend such generate→validate→(repair)→execute workflows but provide limited preregistered, paired measurements of the incremental value contributed by a sandboxed-emulation stage. To narrow that gap we preregistered and executed a paired experiment whose primary question is: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (i) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (ii) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (iii) an evidence-based interpretation for the observed near-zero marginal effect; and (iv) prescriptive boundary conditions and reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.
sections.related_work: Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools have been advocated across recent NetOps and AIOps surveys and system reports because correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional—syntax, ordering, invariants, and runtime dynamics each require different V&V primitives [1]–[3]. Prototype integrations of LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops report heterogeneous gains: in some regimes static checks catch most faults, while in others emulation uncovers subtle stateful failures that static rule-sets miss. This body of work motivates paired designs that isolate the downstream (post‑generation) contribution of guarded stages: by enforcing a shared initial candidate between conditions we isolate only validator-vs‑emulation downstream effects rather than conflating them with generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory plan (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and a planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic missingness handling (up to two deterministic reseeds on parser failures), a repair budget (≤1 repair call per task), and pre-specified paired inference (exact McNemar two-sided test plus a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI; bootstrap resamples = 10000; seed = 1729). The design enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair a single sampled initial candidate (one provider call) was recorded and fed unchanged to both downstream conditions.

Task bank, topology and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory tasks were deterministically generated from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. The bank covered three abstract vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest contained initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit intent, an explicit required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after allowed deterministic reseeds; in the confirmatory execution there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performs vendor‑CLI parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks, workflow-atomicity constraints, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance; scoring is binary under full_intent_constraint_validation. The guarded pipeline runs the baseline validator and then executes the same normalized candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and virtual devices, observes runtime state transitions (interface admin changes, MTU/VLAN applications, transient concurrent states), and maps runtime observations to guarded detections when they contradict policy or reveal safety violations not captured by the validator's static rule-set. The emulation-to-detection mapping is intentionally conservative in this study (emulation flags only clear runtime-policy violations).

Provider-call audit fields: interpretation and provenance. The execution manifest records stage-level provider-call accounting. In our run the manifest reports model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. To avoid confusion: these audited counts enumerate model-call events by pipeline stage ("shared_initial_generation" = calls that produced the single shared candidate for each pair; "repair" = repair-stage calls invoked by the guarded pipeline). They are not per‑condition episode tallies; rather they are call-level counts that explain why model_calls_used exceeds Npairs (one additional repair-stage call occurred). Deterministic reconciliation links these stage-level counts to episode-level contingency results so auditors can locate the exact episode(s) associated with repair-stage activity.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis used a paired-binary executor aligned with McNemar inference and produced an exact two-sided test p-value plus a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory with Bonferroni-adjusted CIs. The primary analysis used complete-pair handling; no irrecoverable technical pairs occurred.
sections.results:
All numeric results below are verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts. Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1; deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 720 and zero failed episodes.

Discordant-pair attribution. With shared_initial_candidate semantics enforced, the unique n10 = 1 discordant pair must stem from (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not captured by the validator, or (ii) the single repair-stage invocation. Deterministic reconciliation and the provider-call audit link the discordant episode to the single recorded repair-stage call; an auditor can locate that episode in the archived raw results for per-episode traces. No additional discordant episodes were observed.
sections.discussion:
Why the near-zero marginal benefit? The archived artifacts support three artifact-grounded factors. First, a validator-ceiling effect: the deterministic validator explicitly encoded the workflow checks exercised by the curated tasks (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore and make_before_break), and most shared_initial candidates already satisfied those rules (representative validator_trace fields show violation_count = 0). With baseline success = 719/720 there is minimal headroom for emulation to add detections. Second, curated inclusion reduced adversarial exposure: parser-validated, deterministically generated tasks bias the confirmatory set toward inputs that a strong validator can handle, underrepresenting runtime-only faults common in noisier or adversarial distributions. Third, the shared_initial_candidate design isolates downstream effects but intentionally removes any guarded benefit that could arise from independent re-generation or more aggressive repair before validator execution.

Operational implications. In pipelines where (a) a high-coverage static validator is maintained and (b) input intents are parser-validated and constrained, an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may provide negligible incremental detection value at scale. That conclusion is narrowly scoped to the experimental regime studied. Guarded emulation remains valuable in broader or risk-sensitive settings: noisy natural-language intents, adversarial misconfigurations, expanded multi-vendor diversity, or long-lived control-plane interactions where emulation can expose behaviors that static rules cannot capture.

Practical recommendations. Operators should (i) invest in validator coverage for common, high-throughput changes when latency and throughput are priorities; (ii) selectively apply guarded sandboxing to high-risk changes or canary deployments where emulation fidelity justifies the cost; (iii) build adversarial/fuzzing task banks to identify validator gaps—our archived traces provide concrete seed cases for such exercises.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured the marginal detection contribution of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-produced NetOps artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and deterministic reconciliation links the unique discordant episode to that single repair invocation. We interpret this near-zero aggregate effect as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated, parser-validated task design. Whether guarded stages add substantive operational value in broader, adversarial, or production-like regimes remains an open empirical question; the archived execution bundle provides reproducible seed artifacts and per-episode traces to support such follow-up work. For independent verification, the archived execution manifest and raw results (execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl in the run bundle) contain the canonical inputs, per-episode traces, and analysis artifacts used to produce these numbers.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: Autonomous post-lock research run executed under the frozen master prompt supplied at autonomy lock. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistered before execution). Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution accounting (artifact-grounded): completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); full execution manifest and per-episode artifacts are archived in the run bundle (see the execution manifest in the archived bundle for full provenance). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Preregistered task bank is synthetic, parser-validated, and deterministic; this creates limited ecological diversity and contributes to a validator-ceiling effect.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) restrict generalizability across model and validator families.
Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream guarded-stage effects but exclude any guarded benefit that could arise from independent re-generation prior to validation.
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity vendor-specific emulators or long-duration stateful tests could change outcomes.

The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.
